definition: Two finite Markov processes can share a one-time stationary law (or a matched stationary occupancy) yet differ in multi-time statistics: passage and first-passage times, episode lifetimes, two-step laws or order. Quantities fixed by the stationary law alone (e.g. Kac set recurrence 1/pi(D)) cannot discriminate them.
label: Occupancy does not fix process
plain_definition: Knowing how often something is the case does not tell you how long it lasts or how it gets there.

definition: A conclusion about a stochastic relational process can change with the time parameterisation (continuous time vs jump/event count vs an epoch counting only some event types) and with the projection used to read it out. The clock is part of the estimand.
label: Clock and readout dependence
plain_definition: What you see depends on how you count time and what you choose to watch.

definition: Whether some record of past events must be added to the current state to predict the future (Markov sufficiency on an augmented state), as distinct from history merely being informative about the past. Includes the compilation question: can a fixed current-state kernel reproduce the history-conditioned law?
label: History as a predictive variable
plain_definition: Sometimes the present snapshot is enough to predict what comes next; sometimes you also need to know how you got here.

definition: A state description (or quotient of it) is predictively sufficient for a declared observable and horizon if conditioning on it renders further past information irrelevant to that observable's future law. Valid dynamical quotients must commute with the kernel (strong lumpability).
label: Future-relative predictive sufficiency
plain_definition: A summary is good enough when adding more detail about the present or past would not improve your forecast of the thing you care about.

definition: Hard constraints change which transitions exist (support, reachable class, one-way transitions); soft constraints change positive rates. Zero lies outside the multiplicative/log-additive weight algebra, yet some stationary observables can be continuous along a ladder of soft factors ending at a hard ban.
label: Admissibility versus weighting
plain_definition: Forbidding something is different in kind from merely making it rare, even when the results sometimes look similar.

definition: Dependence of a lower-order event (a pair toggle) on higher-order current structure: triads, paths, witness counts or hyperedges. Distinct from history and from initial-condition memory.
label: Higher-order and topological context
plain_definition: Whether one link changes can depend on the shape of the links around it.

definition: Long-lived memory of an initial condition or past selection (retention, which decays in an irreducible chain) is distinct from exact dependence of the next event on current structure.
label: Retention versus current dependence
plain_definition: Forgetting where you started is not the same as ignoring where you are now.

definition: Five distinct estimands that are easily conflated: occupancy (one-time stationary mass), passage (hitting/committor/first-passage between declared sets), retention (survival of a configuration or memory), resilience (return after perturbation) and reconstruction (recovery of a configuration after loss). Each needs its own declared source law, clock and control.
label: Retention, resilience, reconstruction, occupancy and passage
plain_definition: How common something is, how you reach it, how long it lasts, whether it bounces back and whether it can be rebuilt are five different questions.

definition: A comparison process declared before results that matches a target on stated quantities (occupancy, density, mean rate, adjacent laws) so that remaining differences are attributable to what is not matched. Matching a quantity also fixes everything that quantity determines (e.g. Kac recurrence, CT edge lifetime).
label: Matched-control design
plain_definition: A fair comparison keeps chosen things equal on purpose, and you must know what else that silently keeps equal.

definition: A stationary chain is reversible iff detailed balance holds (no net cycle currents); a stationary arrow is net irreversible flux. Which rule classes guarantee reversibility depends on label covariance and witness structure.
label: Reversibility and stationary arrow
plain_definition: A process has a direction when, even in balance, it runs around some loops more one way than the other.

definition: An object chosen by an observer for an extreme current property (e.g. the maximum-degree vertex) shows that property at selection time by construction; persistence is the decay of that advantage under the dynamics, against comparators. In finite exchangeable irreducible chains no labelled object stays distinguished.
label: Selection is not persistence
plain_definition: Picking the tallest person in a room does not show that tallness lasts.

definition: GT and CL 8N both descend from CL 8G (22e252e) and share the constraint-lab DSL, kernel builder and coherence validator. Agreement on anything inherited is not independent evidence.
label: Shared code and kernel lineage
plain_definition: Two reports written with the same calculator can agree because of the calculator.

definition: Gravitational attraction as understood in physics. Not a model object in any programme here. It is named only so that tempting but unsupported bridges (false attractors) can be recorded and rejected.
label: Physical gravitational attraction (external notion)
plain_definition: Gravity as physicists mean it, which none of these models derives.
